Proposed controls, grounded in [NextItNet’s causal dilated residual backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163): compare final-layer readout, uniform layer averaging, learned global layer weights, history-dependent gating, and an ungated baseline with useful trainable parameters matched through pointwise layers. Keep dilation schedules, receptive fields, embeddings, loss, sampling, training opportunities and final-nonpadding readout identical. Report parameters and GPU cost. Global weights distinguish learned layer preference from adaptive context selection; replacing trained gates with their training-history mean provides an additional intervention. Gate entropy and history-length associations are diagnostics, not proof. Each variant remains one jointly trained network per category; deploy one checkpoint per category.

For uncertainty, retain paired per-user hit indicators on identical candidates. Report category differences and macro difference Δ = ¼Σc meanᵤ(hit_gate−hit_control). Bootstrap users within each category, preserving model pairs and recomputing the macro difference, for a 95% interval; report discordant wins/losses and exact McNemar tests per category. Apply Holm correction across prespecified comparisons. User-level paired evaluation follows [recommender evaluation guidance](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09371-3). Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on these four datasets, fixed candidates and fitted models—not training-seed variability or full-catalog performance.

Repeated validation optimization can overfit the selection criterion ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Preregister a small comparison set, primary macro HR@10 contrast, checkpoint schedule, stopping rule and GPU allocations within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Keep preprocessing/training/evaluation seeds 0/42/42, epochs ≤200 and batches/epoch 200. Count checkpoint choices and failed runs in the search ledger; report all attempted configurations. Multiplicity correction helps prespecified comparisons but does not remove adaptive selection bias. Without untouched evaluation data, label selected validation gains exploratory; freeze the final configuration before host-only held-out evaluation.
